submission.justification:
Algorithm-L3 (Iterative Topological Clustering with Learned Calibration) at 30 GeV threshold achieves the highest signal efficiency of 90.336% at the allocated 8 kHz trigger rate, representing a substantial improvement over alternatives: +5.49 percentage points over Algorithm-L2 (84.85% @ 40 GeV) and +16.42 percentage points over Algorithm-L1 (73.92% @ 30 GeV).

This recommendation is based on comprehensive simulation testing of 15 configurations (3 algorithms × 5 thresholds from 20-60 GeV, with 100k events per point). Algorithm-L3 consistently outperformed alternatives across the entire threshold range, demonstrating superior clustering and calibration capabilities.

The 30 GeV threshold represents the peak of the efficiency curve for Algorithm-L3, with a broad plateau maintaining >90% efficiency from 30-40 GeV, providing excellent robustness against energy calibration uncertainties and operational variations.

All hardware and operational constraints are satisfied with comfortable margins: FPGA resources explicitly confirmed in specifications, optical bandwidth requirements met for 25 Gb/s links, threshold well within 20-60 GeV range (10 GeV lower margin, 30 GeV upper margin), and performance achieved at exact 8 kHz rate allocation.

The configuration is deployment-ready for the September trigger menu review and Q4 firmware freeze timeline, with Algorithm-L2 @ 40 GeV available as a validated fallback option if needed.
